## Overview

A stock screener is essentially a filter that lets you narrow down the universe of equities based on criteria you define — price, volume, fundamentals, technical indicators, or even sentiment data. Modern screeners go beyond simple tick‑boxes; they incorporate AI‑driven suggestions, real‑time alerts, and seamless integration with brokerage platforms. The goal is to turn raw data into actionable ideas without drowning in spreadsheets.

## Why Use a Stock Screener

Manually scanning thousands of ticker symbols is impractical, especially when market conditions shift by the minute. A screener does the heavy lifting, highlighting only those stocks that meet your predefined rules. This not only speeds up research but also reduces emotional bias — you’re less likely to chase a hot tip when the numbers don’t back it up. For active traders, screeners can trigger intraday alerts; for investors, they help build watchlists for deeper fundamental analysis.

## Top Features to Look For

When evaluating screeners, prioritize real‑time data coverage, customizable filter libraries, and intuitive UI design. Look for the ability to save and share screens, set up email or push notifications, and export results to CSV or directly to your broker. Advanced users appreciate backtesting capabilities, which let you see how a screen would have performed historically. Finally, consider pricing tiers — some platforms offer free basic screens while premium plans unlock deeper fundamentals and AI insights.
